questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Always look in your rearview and side mirrors before changing lanes. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This makes sure no one is passing you or in your blind spot.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Be ready to drive faster than the train.
Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and continue driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train might be coming. Always obey these signs. Never go around lowered gates or ignore the warning sign.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip the road better than when you are driving on pavement.
Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads give your tires less grip than concrete or asphalt. You must slow down on these roads. Stopping takes longer and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: The most common mistake that drivers make when backing is failing to look both ways behind them.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Most drivers fail to look both ways when backing up. Mirrors do not show everything behind you. Turn your body and head to look through the rear window to see as much as possible.

questions.question: When taking any medicine, you should:

options.text: Consult your doctor about the effects before driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive more slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Consult your doctor about the effects before driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before driving if you take any medicine. This is especially important if you are taking tranquilizers or sedatives.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Warns you about conditions on or near the road.
Helps direct you to cities and towns ahead.
Tells you about traffic laws and regulations.
Tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns you about conditions on or near the road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert you about road conditions ahead. These signs are usually diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers maintaining a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always follow the speed limit and slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: The faster the speed of your vehicle, the longer it takes to stop when you must react to other drivers' unexpected movements.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: When you drive faster, it takes longer to stop. This is why you need more time to react when other drivers make sudden moves.

questions.question: What might happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?

options.text: The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be increased.
Nothing will happen.
The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be reduced.
The effects of only the alcohol may be reduced.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be increased.
questions.explanation: When you mix alcohol with another drug, both effects can become stronger. For example, one drink taken with a cold medicine may affect you like you had several drinks.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, it is important to remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.
Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.
Require less time to pass on an incline than smaller vehicles do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
questions.explanation: Trucks are large and heavy. They need much longer distances to stop than smaller cars.

questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, what should you do?

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must always yield the right-of-way to them.

questions.question: When a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right side of the road.
Stop your vehicle as far away from traffic as possible.
Turn off your engine, radio, and any other device that may interfere with hearing the officer.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right side of the road and stop as far from traffic as possible. Turn off your engine, radio, and other devices so you can hear the officer clearly.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. You must stop for them, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time will lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers will not reduce your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?

options.text: During the night.
During the day.
Under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under ideal conditions. Always drive at a safe speed based on weather, traffic, and road conditions.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.
Where there is a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a red traffic light. You must also always obey orders from police officers directing traffic.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Allow additional distance between your vehicle and the vehicles ahead.
Approach all vehicles with caution.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your following distance because slippery roads require more space to stop. Drive cautiously around all vehicles.

questions.question: How can you identify an aggressive driver?

options.text: By their erratic and improper lane changes.
By the number of passengers in their car.
By their tendency to drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: By their erratic and improper lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch for aggressive drivers making erratic or improper lane changes. The safest action is to stay out of their way.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly turn before the truck or bus does.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit between a turning truck or bus and the curb. Wait until it completes its turn to avoid a serious crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right.
Double curve.
Winding road.
Pavement ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has many turns or curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic may be coming toward you from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are making a turn.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly at all times when driving.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should put on your cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal tells you to. Always be careful when driving near railroad tracks.

questions.question: Tailgating other drivers (driving too closely to their rear bumper):

options.text: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
Cannot result in a traffic citation.
Reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is unsafe behavior that can lead to aggressive driving. You should avoid it. Drivers can face legal consequences for unsafe driving.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway:

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Continue to the next exit and turn around safely.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines mark the center of the road and separate lanes of traffic, passing is:

options.text: Permitted from the left.
Permitted from the right.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean that drivers going in both directions cannot cross the centerline to pass.

questions.question: When an authorized vehicle using its sirens and flashing lights approaches a vehicle, the driver should pull to the right-hand edge of the roadway and wait for the emergency vehicle to pass.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens approaches you, you must move to the right side of the road and let it pass.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Can make turning more difficult.
Are likely to hydroplane.
Can increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires make turning harder and increase your stopping distance. Tires without good tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.
Ensure that your tires are properly inflated.
Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with good tread depth and proper inflation. Slow down when driving in the rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at higher speeds.

questions.question: When a stop line is present at a stop sign, drivers must stop:

options.text: At the line.
On top of the line.
Only if pedestrians are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the line.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign with a stop line, you must stop before the line or crosswalk. Go when the way is clear.
